cells.tense: You are keeping the picture clear and saying it at the depth this moment can take.
cells.ask: Think of one true sentence you said this week that landed well, and write down what let you pitch it that way.
cells.core:
You know how to see what's going on and how to put it in front of someone at a depth they can take. Not everything at once. Not softened into nothing. Right at the edge of what the moment can carry — a skill most people do not bother to build.

Right now you are doing it well. You won't pretend a guess is a fact, and you won't say the true thing so hard it stops being useful. That balance is the whole craft. Nothing needs pushing today. Stay where you are and keep telling the truth at the depth the room can receive.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the picture clear and pitch it where it lands.
cells.verb: keeping perception clear, and saying so at the right depth
cells.place: the open expanse before any one thing has been chosen

cells.tense: You are preparing for a conversation that hasn't started, writing lines they may not say.
cells.ask: Choose one talk you're dreading and prepare nothing for it — no opening, no rebuttal, no ending — then answer only what is actually said.
cells.core:
You've already mapped how the talk will go, what you'll say when they push back, which version of the truth will land better. None of it has happened. The preparing is running ahead of the thing being prepared for, and that gap is where you live now.

What has no room is the part that can't be written in advance: hearing the other person and answering what is actually there. You're so far into the next version that the live one doesn't get your attention. Let the conversation arrive before you decide what it is. The lines will come when there's a mouth saying them.
cells.sheetLine: You've written the whole talk before they've said a word.

cells.tense: You are holding what you see close, not offering it, keeping the picture to yourself.
cells.ask: Send one person one clear, small thing you noticed — just the single observation, and let them do whatever they do with it.
cells.core:
You still catch what's off in a room. You still know what wants naming. None of that has gone anywhere. What's missing is the step toward a person — the offer, the saying out loud, the hand-off. What you see stays on the shelf.

Seeing a thing clearly and putting it in front of someone are two different acts, and it's the second one that's quiet right now. The first one is fine on its own. Start with something small enough that a person can hold it, with someone who will take it as offered. What you see only does its work once it leaves your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it. You've stopped handing it over.

cells.tense: You are keeping the room clear right now, and talking about it as if the room did that by itself.
cells.ask: After one conversation today, say plainly to yourself, 'I kept that clear,' and let that be true without adding a reason it doesn't count.
cells.core:
You notice when a smooth sentence is hiding an agenda. You catch the misread before it hardens. You say the difficult thing kindly enough for someone to hear it. All of that runs through how you are with people, and you describe it as reading the room or just being careful.

What's left out isn't the work — it's that you are the one doing it. You talk as if the clarity belongs to the room, and you happen to be standing in it. Saying it once plainly, to yourself, keeps it yours. The next room you walk into will be built the same way, whether you name the builder or not.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping it clear, and you call it being careful.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that at Balanced the person is already 'holding clear sight for other people' — the record gives the capacity, not the history or the audience. A reader could reasonably say they have no one around them in that role, or that the holding exhausts them some days; both can stand against the core without emptying the ask. The ask survives being wrong: marking one true sentence that landed is useful whether or not my read fits, because it only needs the sentence and the noticing. The sentence that serves me more than them would be 'you have the gift of seeing clearly' — a line that flatters the writer and hands over nothing, so it is cut.
